title: Message Brokers and Queues
unclear_source_points: The course uses 'message queue' and 'message broker' interchangeably for intuition; it does not distinguish the broker process from the queues, exchanges, and bindings the broker manages.

The generic read-then-delete explanation primarily matches Amazon SQS visibility and deletion semantics. The instructor explicitly notes that RabbitMQ differs but does not spell out RabbitMQ's manual acknowledgement and connection-close redelivery behavior.

The course says a redelivered message reappears at the head of the queue. Exact placement and ordering after requeue are broker, queue-type, concurrency, and timing dependent, so this is not a portable ordering guarantee.
The exercise asks the learner to explore features and guarantees without naming a bounded feature set, proof method, message schema, failure experiment, cost limit, or cleanup procedure.
The optional SQS substitution is conditional on authorized AWS access; the source does not require creating or changing a cloud account when that access is absent.
